fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. When the land is divided by lot as an inheritance, the LORD says, "…you are to set aside a portion for the LORD, a holy portion of the land…" (Ezekiel 45:1). Before anybody gets a slice, a portion is already marked for Him.

The elders aren't named in this verse, friend. The strip is for the priests who minister in the sanctuary (Ezekiel 45:4). It holds their houses and the holy area for the sanctuary. No elders are on the list here.

That's right, baker. The adjacent area "…shall belong to the Levites who minister in the temple…" (Ezekiel 45:5). It's their possession, and the towns where they live go there. Priests on one side, Levites on the other, and the sanctuary right nearby. I'd never have to hunt for a neighbor to borrow a mixing bowl from!

Royal sounds fancy, baker, but this verse doesn't ask for fancy. It says, "You must use honest scales, a just ephah, and a just bath." (Ezekiel 45:10). Honest means the measure is true. The word isn't "royal."

The long list of offerings can make a sentence like this one look tricky, friend. But the text ends the sentence with the purpose: "…to make atonement for the house of Israel." (Ezekiel 45:17). So the offerings the prince provides are for atonement. That makes this one true.

You've got it, baker. The Lord GOD says, "…take a young bull without blemish and purify the sanctuary." (Ezekiel 45:18). A young bull without blemish is the offering for it. That's for the first day of the first month.

I can see why you'd think so, baker, but that isn't what the text says. The seventh-day offering is "…for anyone who strays unintentionally or in ignorance." (Ezekiel 45:20). Those are the two cases the text names. Stray on purpose isn't one of them.

That's right, baker. The offering is done "…for anyone who strays unintentionally or in ignorance." (Ezekiel 45:20). Those are the two cases the text names. In this way atonement is made for the temple.
